adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py:1048 — Dropping ifNull(sample_weight, 1) makes sum() skip events with NULL sample_weight (e.g. events ingested before a project was allowlisted), so upsampled counts silently undercount or come back NULL/0 for historical buckets.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `upsampled_count` in `discover.py` as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with no null-coalescing. The finding’s specific risk (NULL `sample_weight` leading to ignored rows / undercount) is grounded in this new implementation. However, the diff also explicitly documents an assumption that `sample_weight` exists for all events in allowlisted projects (“no additional null checks are needed here”), and it does not show whether `sample_weight` can be NULL for historical events. So the concern is a real robustness/edge-case issue created by the change, but it’s not verifiably a defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:77 — Removing convert_fields_for_upsampling, UPSAMPLED_ERROR_AGGREGATION, the include_alias kwarg and upsampled_eps/upsampled_epm will break any other callers, such as the organization events endpoint, with ImportError/TypeError or an unknown-function error; the sparse test suite cannot catch this.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show any removal of `convert_fields_for_upsampling`, `UPSAMPLED_ERROR_AGGREGATION`, an `include_alias` kwarg, or `upsampled_eps/upsampled_epm`. Instead, it *adds* a new helper module (`src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`), adds an `upsampled_count` SnQL function in `discover.py`, and updates `organization_events_stats.py` to call the new helper functions. Since the alleged removals and resulting ImportError/TypeError/unknown-function failures are not evidenced in this diff, the finding misreads changes not present here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:92 — Only count() is upsampled now, so a chart with yAxis=[count(), epm()/eps()] mixes upsampled counts with raw rates, and sample_count()/sample_eps()/sample_epm() no longer map to the raw values.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling()` only rewrites the exact expression `count()` into `upsampled_count() as count` (src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py). In `organization_events_stats.py`, that transform is applied to the entire `query_columns` list (`final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)`), meaning mixed yAxes like `["count()", "epm()"]` would result in an upsampled count alongside an unmodified second metric. The diff does not show whether `epm()`/`eps()` (or any other aggregations) should also be upsampled, so the claim about “raw rates” and `sample_count()/sample_eps()/sample_epm()` mapping cannot be strictly verified here, but the review concern about incomplete/partial transformation across multi-axis queries is grounded in the code change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:38 — The eligibility cache stays stale for up to 60s after an allowlist change, and there are no cache-hit or staleness tests, so a request can upsample or not based on a stale allowlist while tests stay green (options are mocked and the cache is real).

adjudication.rationale: In `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` the allowlist eligibility result is cached for 60s (`cache.set(cache_key, is_eligible, 60)`), so an allowlist change can take up to 60s to affect behavior unless `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is called (it’s defined but not used anywhere in this diff). The added tests mock `options.get` but do not exercise cache-hit behavior or staleness/invalidation; they also don’t control/patch `cache`, so they won’t validate the caching semantics. The staleness itself appears to be an intentional tradeoff per the docstring, so it’s more of a coverage/operational concern than a guaranteed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:67 — invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called and is keyed on one exact project set, so an allowlist change cannot invalidate the many other cached project-set keys for the org; the invalidation is effectively dead.

adjudication.rationale: In the added helper module, `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)` is defined but there are no call sites in the provided diff (no references from `organization_events_stats.py` or tests), so it is currently dead/unused. Also, both caching and invalidation use a cache key that includes a hash of the *entire sorted project_ids set* (`hash(tuple(sorted(...)))`), meaning invalidating one exact project-set key would not clear other cached combinations for the same org. This is a real, diff-grounded design/maintainability concern around cache invalidation strategy, but not a directly verifiable correctness break since the cache TTL is 60s and the feature can still function without explicit invalidation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:27 — The added cache.get/cache.set round-trip to the shared cache on every stats request is probably slower than the options.get it replaces (options are already cached in-process), so the "performance optimization" may add latency and cache churn.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a shared-cache lookup and write in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (`cache.get(cache_key)` then `cache.set(..., 60)`) for eligibility on every stats request path that reaches this helper. This introduces an external cache round-trip and potential churn (many keys via `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`) where previously the allowlist check would just be an `options.get(...)` call. Whether it is actually slower depends on runtime characteristics not shown in the diff, but the concern is specific and grounded in the new code and is an architecture/performance tradeoff rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:27 — The cache key uses the 64-bit Python hash() of the project-id tuple instead of the ids themselves, so two different project sets in the same org can collide and share a cached eligibility result.

adjudication.rationale: In `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` the cache key is built as `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"`. Because this uses Python’s `hash()` of the project-id tuple rather than a collision-free encoding of the IDs, two distinct project-id sets can theoretically produce the same hash value and therefore share a cache entry, leading to an incorrect cached eligibility result being reused for the wrong project set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:63 — The switch from ANY to ALL means adding one non-allowlisted project (or selecting all projects) silently turns off upsampling for every allowlisted project in the query, so counts drop about 10x with no signal to the user.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly implements and documents an ALL-projects allowlist gate: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` returns `all(project_id in allowlist for project_id in project_ids)`, and `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` only enables the `count()` -> `upsampled_count()` transformation when that is true. As a result, adding any non-allowlisted project to the query disables upsampling for the entire query, which can materially reduce counts for allowlisted projects (tests in `test_organization_events_stats.py` even assert this behavior in the “partial allowlist” case).
